source_inspection.mango_limit: Three historical load events at different operations; no linked consumption, intervention assignment or repeated site-cluster series.

assumptions.model: normal estimator with known, fixed standard error and symmetric two-sided CI

independent_review: A read-only reviewer confirmed the normal-model formulas and explicit non-field classification, then found two extreme-precision false accepts: a very small standard error could round the required effect to the threshold, and a near-certain target could allow a failure probability millions of times larger than requested. The script now round-trips both success and failure tails and rejects unrepresentable effects; both negative CLI regressions pass.
limits: The standard error is hypothetical, chosen to show approximately 80 percent probability for a two-sided difference-from-zero event under a fixed-SE normal model; it is not estimated from field data.

The 2.5 percent success-bound probability applies only to the specified symmetric, calibrated normal interval when the assumed true effect equals the threshold; it is not an estimate for a cluster-bootstrap interval.
No site-specific V inputs, between-cluster variance, intracluster correlation, stratum/volume adjustment, contamination or planned randomization were modeled.

The field-design preflight requires declared observations and does not certify prospective power. A competent human must approve the decision event and design assumptions before any cluster assignment.
No field intervention, causal effect, adverse-event assessment or criterion-3 acceptance was produced.
